question: How does the Lord's freedom manifest as knowledge, memory, removal, and world-creation?
premises: The Lord dwells in the heart of all.
From the Lord come memory, knowledge, and removal.
The Lord alone is to be known by all Vedas and Vedanta.
The Lord's nature is independent knowing whose essence is the heart's all-removal.
Reflection 'there I am' is knowledge made of new manifestation and world-creation.
Conceptual knowledge is removal, bond-creation, maya-made cognizer-fixation.
Remembering is the residue of latent impressions of what was led and withdrawn, manifesting again.
By this all knowledges are withdrawn, and agency as freedom preceded by omniscience is declared.
All scriptures determine the supreme Lord-principle alone.
The Lord's freedom is world-agency through creating and uprooting the world and establishing own nature.
Others make removal by difference-cognition, producing Vedanta and Veda through self-realization.
inference: The verse identifies the Lord's svatantrya as the single ground of knowing, remembering, removing, and creating the world.
uncertainties: The compound glosses are highly compressed and some readings may be corrupt or interpretive.
The exact doctrinal referents of 'removal' and 'bond-creation' are not fully recoverable from this line alone.
plain_english: I dwell in the heart of all; from me come memory, knowledge, and removal. I alone am known by all the Vedas and Vedanta. The knowable nature is independent knowing, and the reflection 'there I am' is knowledge as new manifestation and world-creation. Conceptual knowledge is removal, bond-creation, and maya-made fixation; remembering is the residue of withdrawn impressions manifesting again. Thus all knowledges are withdrawn, and agency as freedom preceded by omniscience is declared. All scriptures determine the supreme Lord-principle alone; the Lord's freedom is world-agency through creating, uprooting, and re-establishing own nature. Others, by difference-cognition, make removal and thereby produce Vedanta and Veda through self-realization.
